content: More than 100 Debian packages retained distrusted CA certificates after updates, affecting applications that rely on their own trust stores. Debian developers are discussing potential solutions. Administrators must ensure their systems use the latest ca-certificates update and check trust settings in various applications.
title: Over 100 Debian Packages Still Contain Distrusted CA Certificates Despite Security Updates

content: Microsoft is investigating issues with attachment uploads in New Outlook, while uploads in Outlook on the web and classic Outlook are unaffected. Users can switch to these alternatives or wait for the fix. The impact is limited, and no regions or user counts are specified. The issue is being tracked in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1561765.
title: Microsoft Investigates Attachment Upload Failures in New Outlook
Dutch Data Protection Authority Warns of Safety Risks in AI Smart Glasses
content: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) warns against buying AI-powered smart glasses due to safety issues, including incorrect advice and privacy risks. Tests revealed misinterpretations of safety warnings, potential data processing outside EU, and the ability for nearby individuals to connect to and view recordings without permission. AP advises politicians to consider policy development for high-risk AI products.

title: Behind the Blog: Keeping It Together
content: This week's Behind the Blog discusses online discourse toxicity, focusing on the public's sudden interest in a hippo situation at a zoo, leading to a surge in amateur expertise and heated debate. No technical impact reported, but highlights the impact of online discourse on public interest and community dynamics.

title: Moxa issues security advisory for multiple product series
content: Moxa announces vulnerabilities in several product series, including ioLogik E1200, EDS-E, IKS, ICS, PT, SDS, TWS, and TN. Affected firmware versions are all prior to v4.0. Users are advised to update to the latest firmware to mitigate potential exploits.

Centralized password management improves credential visibility, identifies security risks, and simplifies secure password sharing. IT administrators using spreadsheets are at risk of weak, reused, or compromised credentials.

title: Critical Apache Tomcat Flaw Allows Remote Attackers to Join Server Clusters Without Authentication
content: A critical flaw in Apache Tomcat, tracked as CVE-2026-133325, allows remote attackers to join trusted server clusters without authentication. Affects versions 11.0.28-29, 10.1.62, and 9.0.124. Requires TLS 1.3 with a pre-shared key. Mitigation: Switch to TLS 1.2 with the pre-shared key enabled.

title: Signal restricts screenshots to prevent AI assistants from accessing private chats
content: Signal is updating its iOS and Android apps to block screenshots to prevent AI assistants like Siri and Gemini from accessing private conversations. This update aims to protect user privacy by preventing AI systems from reading chats.

title: US Launches Threat Disruption Center to Combat Scams
content: The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to coordinate efforts between investigators and companies to disrupt scam networks targeting Americans. It aims to warn victims sooner, pause payments, and freeze funds. Victims should report scams promptly to the FBI’s IC3 to maximize the chance of recovering lost funds.

The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies to help prevent scams, freeze funds, and take down malicious infrastructure. content: Hackers deployed a malware campaign called CyberLeek using over 355 domains to distribute fake GTA 6 PC launchers, which deliver malicious software. The campaign targets gamers looking for early releases. Visitors may download a ZIP archive containing a disguised installer. Mitigation includes deleting unopened files and checking for unusual activity if the installer was run.
title: Hackers Use 355 Domains to Spread Fake GTA 6 PC Launchers Delivering Malware

content: A ransomware group leaked personal information, including emails and phone numbers, from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase customers. No payment data was reported exposed, but the data could be used by scammers. JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed incidents involving third-party providers. Customers are advised to verify messages and use official channels to protect accounts.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers
Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers
content: A ransomware group leaked data including emails, phone numbers, and travel/dining bookings from third-party service providers of Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. No payment data was exposed. Companies acknowledged incidents but reported no impact on their payment networks. Customers are advised to verify messages independently and consider credit freezes for identity protection.

Hackers rebuilt the SoftEther VPN Bridge, renaming it NtMonitor, to facilitate stealthy access to government networks. Webworm, a China-aligned espionage group, used this tool to maintain post-breach access without triggering standard security measures. Researchers from Rapid7 identified the modified tool and provided guidance on detection and mitigation.
title: Hackers Turn Legitimate VPN Software Into a Stealthy Tool for Spying on Government Networks
OpenSSL Hit by Critical 9.8 Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in Base64 Encoding Function
content: A heap buffer overflow in OpenSSL’s Base64 encoding function can corrupt application memory when processing large inputs. The vulnerability (CVE-2026-121481) affects OpenSSL versions 4.0.0 to 4.0.3 and 4.1.0. Security teams should check for large untrusted data use and enforce input limits. Update to OpenSSL 4.0.4 or 4.1.1 to mitigate risk.

A vulnerability in KVM allowed researchers to access 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from a guest VM. Affects AMD hosts with nested virtualization enabled. Mitigation involves updating to fixed kernels.
title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
AI Autonomy Gains Traction in Security Operations Centers
content: Security leaders plan to increase AI autonomy in SOC, with 60% expecting full comfort in autonomously acting on low-risk security actions within 12 months. This initiative is the top ranking for 2027. The technical impact includes enhanced automation and potentially reduced human oversight.

title: UK Court Confirms Demand for Apple iCloud Backdoor
content: The UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN) demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data, contradicting the NCND policy. Apple revoked Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users, while US officials urged opposition. The court has not disclosed the TCN's precise content, citing national security concerns. A substantive hearing is scheduled for 2027.

title: BYOD Ransomware Hackers Play Audio Ransom Messages on Computers Across Hospitals and Universities
content: Ransomware hackers played audio ransom messages on computers in hospitals and universities, affecting the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center and Vanderbilt University. The incidents disrupted operations, with ambulances diverted and clinics canceling appointments. BYOD claimed to compromise 36,000 systems, though this remains unverified. Universities warned of unexpected login prompts and advised password resets. The technical impact included unexpected audio playback and repeated login requests. Mitigation focused on endpoint security and user education.

title: Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX Framework to Automate Cyberattacks Without Relying on Zero-Day Exploits
content: Attackers are using an AI-driven tool called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks by hunting for ordinary security mistakes and continuously acting on them. This has led to rapid unauthorized access in under three hours. The framework is open-source and connects a large language model to hacking tools, enabling automated decision-making and actions. Defenders should limit access to exposed tools and APIs, set strict API controls, and test unusual API usage. Indicators of compromise include backdoored Docker images and specific user agents.

title: Windows 11 passkey bug causes authentication failure
content: A Windows 11 passkey bug leads to authentication failure messages on Android devices even after successful sign-ins. A fix is available for versions 25H2 and 26H2. Affects Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, but not iPhone users. Until patched, users should ignore Android error messages if sign-in is successful on the PC.

title: SonicWall Warns of Security Risks for Unsupported Gen 6 Firewalls
content: SonicWall advises replacing Generation 6 firewalls due to security risks from AI-assisted attacks. Retiring these devices is crucial to avoid exploitation of critical flaws. Customers are urged to replace and secure their devices promptly.

Threat actors exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway, breaching four devices and accessing an internal network. CVSS score 9.8. A PoC was released shortly before the breach.
title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
BADBOX 3.0 malware used Android TV boxes for ad fraud
content: BADBOX 3.0 malware compromised Android TV boxes to generate 40 billion daily bid requests for ad fraud. Advertisers paid for placements on home internet connections. Mitigation involved disrupting the operation.

Article emphasizes the value of diverse career paths in technology, promoting resilience, curiosity, and inclusivity through community support. No technical incident or cybersecurity threat mentioned.

content: The Digital Café assists the Nauheim community in building tech confidence. Sophos volunteers contribute 40 hours each to support digital inclusion. No technical impact or mitigation described.

content: A critical Java vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) affects Palo Alto Networks' Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector, and on-premises HTML5 Gateway. Successful exploitation could lead to remote code execution. Customers are advised to update to specific versions or later to mitigate the risk.
title: Palo Alto Confirms Critical Java Vulnerability Affects Privilege Threat Analytics and Remote Access Connector
ClamAV Patches 10 High-Severity Vulnerabilities That Could Let Attackers Crash Antivirus Scanners
content: ClamAV released updates to fix 10 high-severity vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to crash antivirus scanners, trap scan workers in endless loops, or drain system resources. The patches address memory errors and affect various file handling components. Administrators should update to ClamAV 1.5.5 or 1.4.7 for protection.

title: UK tribunal confirms secret Apple order in iCloud encryption dispute
content: The UK’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal ordered the Home Office to reveal a secret order seeking access to encrypted iCloud data, impacting Apple users. Technical impact includes potential breach of user privacy and data security. Further legal and technical implications to be determined.

title: Signal Restricts Screenshots to Protect User Privacy from AI Assistants
content: Signal is restricting screenshots on iOS 27 and some Android devices to prevent built-in AI assistants from accessing private chats. The change targets Siri and assistants like Google Gemini, protecting messages from being seen by AI through screen captures. Users can turn off the protection but may expose other messages. Signal is advocating for clearer developer options to control AI access without disabling features.

Hackers exploited misconfigured Temenos Quantum Fabric to gain admin access without passwords, deploying malicious Java components. Affected banks across multiple regions. Malware, named FabricShell and FabricShadow, provided command execution and data exfiltration capabilities. Forescout advises restricting internet access and checking for implants.
title: Hackers Exploit Misconfigured Temenos Banking Platform to Deploy Web Shells Without Passwords

content: Transport for London (TfL) detected a data breach on its Oyster photocard website, exposing personal information such as email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth of 265,000 customers. Passwords and payment card details were not compromised. TfL advised affected customers to change matching passwords or security answers on other accounts. The breach highlights the risk of exposed security questions and answers being reused.
title: Hackers Breach TfL Oyster Photocard Accounts, Exposing Personal Data of 265,000 Customers
Chase Announces Vendor Cyberattack May Have Exposed Customer Data
content: JPMorgan Chase reports attackers targeted third-party vendors, potentially exposing customers’ names and email addresses. Visa and Mastercard also disclosed incidents after data theft by a non-extortion group. Mitigation involves assessing vendor security and enhancing data protection measures.

title: Hackers Actively Scan LiteLLM AI Servers for Critical Flaws Enabling RCE Attacks
content: Hackers are scanning LiteLLM AI servers for two critical flaws, CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710, which together enable remote code execution. The attacks target unpatched versions of LiteLLM, often found between apps and AI model providers, potentially exposing API keys and other secrets. Teams are advised to upgrade to the latest versions and secure their servers. The technical impact is high, with successful exploitation leading to significant access and potential financial loss.

A cryptographer warns that AI advancements may undermine public-key cryptography systems, posing a 15% risk of losing confidence in existing encryption algorithms. Industry experts debate the need for improved cryptographic agility and caution against hasty changes. Mathematical problems traditionally solved by humans are now being outperformed by AI, raising concerns about cryptographic vulnerabilities.
title: AI Advances Spark Debate on Public-Key Cryptography Security

title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deploy RAT to Spy and Control PCs

content: Wireshark 4.6.10 addresses 39 security vulnerabilities, including crashes, processing loops, memory leaks, and heap disclosure issues affecting protocol dissectors and capture file parsers. The update is crucial for network troubleshooting and security analysis, with CVEs like CVE-2026-130455 and CVE-2026-130449 addressing critical flaws. Teams should prioritize updating to mitigate risks.
title: Wireshark 4.6.10 Released to Patch 39 Security Vulnerabilities
Hackers Deploy AI-Assisted PowerShell Toolkit on African Stock Exchange
content: Hackers used an AI-assisted PowerShell toolkit with 41 modules to search for credentials and test access to APIs on a major African stock exchange. The activity, conducted on September 20, 2026, aimed to gain unauthorized access to financial and cloud systems. Security researchers identified six implants linked to Witchetty, a China-linked espionage group. Investigators recommend monitoring DNS queries, API accesses, and endpoint logs for indicators of compromise.

title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
content: China-nexus group Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day in VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890) for admin access and data theft. Technical impact: authentication bypass in VMware Directory Service. Mitigation: Apply patches promptly.

Hackers published customer data from Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan after cyberattacks on third-party service providers. No breaches occurred at the financial companies themselves. Data exposure included names, email addresses, and marketing details. Companies are investigating vendor breaches and offering support to affected customers.
title: Hackers Leak Customer Data Linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan After Third-Party Cyberattacks
Drupal Fixes Critical RCE Flaw Exploitable by Unauthenticated Hackers
content: Drupal fixed a critical RCE flaw in the installer that could allow unauthenticated attackers to take over vulnerable sites. The bug, CVE-2026-132165, affects Drupal core versions 11.3.x, 11.4.x, and 10.6.x. Administrators should update to 11.3.22, 11.4.13, or 10.6.22 to mitigate risks. The update also addresses a separate moderately critical issue.

title: New Unpatched Windows Zero-Day Vulnerability FastUnlock Disclosed
content: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock allows physical access attackers to run programs on a locked Windows machine without signing in. The attacker gains only a limited account. The vulnerability was posted by researchers MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and flagged by ThreatLocker.

A zero-day flaw in Microsoft’s Windows Package Manager (WinGet) allowed a single pull request to potentially compromise moderator GitHub access tokens. This could enable attackers to deploy malicious software updates, access corporate repositories, and steal secrets. Microsoft has patched the issue but advises limiting token scope and validating hosts before attaching credentials. Enterprises must scrutinize internal tools and scripts to mitigate risks.
title: Critical zero-click vulnerability in Microsoft’s WinGet exposes GitHub tokens

content: KPMG Canada confirmed an unauthorized third party accessed confidential tax documents of some clients. Immediate action was taken to secure systems, but details of the breach, including extent and nature of data accessed, remain unclear. Clients should inquire about specific risks to their files.
title: KPMG Canada Confirms Cyberattack on Client Tax Documents
8.8 Million NGINX Services Potentially Exposed to Critical NGINX2Root Vulnerability
content: Around 8.8 million NGINX services are potentially exposed to five memory bugs, allowing unauthenticated users to run commands as a worker process. The most severe bug, CVE-2026-123007, affects versions from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8. Servers must be patched or HTTP/2 disabled to mitigate risk. Censys tracks over 331 million NGINX properties, with 8,823,450 still running affected versions. No exploitation in the wild as of 18 November.

title: European Commission HR Systems Hit by Cyber Attack
content: The European Commission was targeted by cyber attackers using the ARTEX tool, shutting down HR systems for over 10 days. No data breach was confirmed, but access controls were compromised. Mitigation included temporarily disabling applications. HR systems are valuable targets for espionage and social engineering.

title: Hackers Exploit VMware vCenter 0-Day Since September to Hijack Admin Accounts and Steal VM Data
content: A suspected China-linked espionage group exploited a VMware vCenter Server zero-day in September 2026, gaining admin access and stealing VM data. The flaw affects VMware Directory Service, allowing networked attackers to bypass authentication. Mitigation involves patching, restricting access, and reviewing logs for signs of compromise.

VMware issued critical advisories for two vulnerabilities, one allowing unauthorized access to vCenter and the other enabling command execution in SDDC Manager. Apache in Cloud Foundation products also has a remote code execution flaw. KVM disclosed a guest-to-host memory corruption vulnerability affecting AMD processors using nested virtualization. Mitigation involves disabling nested virtualization or applying vendor updates.
title: VMware and KVM Vulnerabilities Exploited in Cloud and Virtual Infrastructure
New Windows 11 Narrator Lock Screen 0-Day Allows Attackers to Bypass BitLocker Protections
content: A newly disclosed Windows 11 zero-day called FastUnlock lets attackers bypass BitLocker protections with physical access. It targets the Narrator screen reader, allowing code execution before sign-in. Mitigation involves limiting physical access to devices.

title: Germ Network Launches Android Messaging Client with End-to-End Encryption
content: Germ Network launched its encrypted messaging client, Germ DM, on Android, seeing a 20x jump in usage. The app uses end-to-end encryption built on Messaging Layer Security and a unique card-based identity system. Bluesky promotes the app for E2E DMs, aiding marketing efforts. Germ aims to offer smart tools for managing social and work life while prioritizing privacy and security.

title: AWS re:Invent 2026 Security Conference
content: The AWS Security, Identity, and Governance team hosts re:Invent 2026, focusing on security in the agentic enterprise era. It features over 120 sessions, keynotes, and workshops addressing identity, detection, network protection, and governance. Attendees can participate in hands-on sessions and meet with AWS experts to discuss security challenges.

content: Technical segments on setting up Waydroid and Mitmproxy, along with news on AI in pentesting, RCE vulnerabilities, and AI challenges for defenders. Vulnerability disclosures and exploits continue to rise, with cloud hosts and VMs under threat.

Multiple vulnerabilities in Google Chrome could allow for arbitrary code execution. Successful exploitation could lead to installation of programs, data modification, or creation of new accounts with full user rights. Users with administrative privileges are more at risk.

OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group Workshop at Open Source Summit Europe
content: The OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group held a workshop at Open Source Summit Europe to discuss cybersecurity policy, focusing on the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). Key areas of discussion included due diligence, vulnerability reporting, and collaboration between manufacturers and maintainers. Participants highlighted the need for practical guidance and tools to address the challenges posed by the CRA.

Third-party breaches at JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard may have exposed customer names and email addresses. No payment data was affected. Financial firms are investigating but declined to disclose further details on the breach or the affected third-party providers.

content: AWS has introduced a new security analytics dashboard for AWS WAF to help investigate traffic and contain threats more efficiently. The dashboard provides a unified view across multiple protection packs and dimensions, enabling faster threat response and reducing false positives. It allows filtering, grouping, and detailed inspection of traffic data.
title: Introducing the New AWS WAF Security Analytics Dashboard

content: A severe authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890) in VMware vCenter was patched, enabling unauthorized access. Patches are available for VMware vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, and 8.0 U3m. Other issues include SQL injection, command injection, privilege escalation, and SAML token bypass vulnerabilities, rated from Important to Moderate. Immediate patching is advised.
title: Critical flaw in VMware vCenter allows authentication bypass
Third-Party JavaScript Compromise Compromises Multiple Websites
content: A recent supply-chain attack exploited a weakness in a vendor’s platform, modifying third-party JavaScript to steal payment card details, tamper with cryptocurrency transactions, and send cookies to attacker-controlled servers. Multiple websites of well-known brands were affected. Mitigation involves a strict Content Security Policy, inventorying third-party scripts, and monitoring changes.

title: Third-Party JavaScript Compromise Affects Multiple Organizations
content: Visitors to websites of well-known brands were served malicious JavaScript via a third-party web service, stealing payment card details and tampering with cryptocurrency transactions. Organizations did not deploy bad code themselves but relied on a vendor’s platform. Content Security Policy (CSP) with strict script-src settings could prevent attacks. Organizations should inventory third-party scripts, enforce CSP, and monitor for changes.

A Russian national, Igor D’iu, was indicted for surveilling employees of a Silicon Valley company assisting Ukraine. He photographed employees and their screens, tracked home addresses, and followed a worker, causing emotional distress. The incident highlights cyber espionage risks in tech and defense sectors.
title: Russian Spy Indicted for Surveillance of Silicon Valley Tech and Defense Company

Deepfake Elon Musk scam nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto
content: A fake Elon Musk livestream tricked Coinbase users into sending $4.7 million in crypto to scammers. Scammers used a deepfake to impersonate Musk, prompting users to send cryptocurrency. Automated defenses stopped about 91% of the attempted transfers. To avoid such scams, users should be wary of unsolicited payment requests, especially those linked to celebrity impersonations.

title: PHP's phpAfterShell Flaw Exposed: Object Injection Leads to Code Execution
content: A vulnerability in PHP's file-based session storage allows object injection, enabling code execution. Affected are users of PHP applications. Mitigation: Update to fixed PHP releases. Technical Impact: Severe, as it bypasses security measures. Response: Apply updates immediately.

title: Fake Elon Musk livestream scam nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto
content: A deepfake of Elon Musk was used in a crypto scam, tricking Coinbase users into sending $4.7 million in attempts. The scam relied on convincing victims to send cryptocurrency to a fake address, bypassing automated defenses. Users were logged in and confirmed the transactions themselves. To stay safe, avoid sending funds to unverified sources and check offers critically.

title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in NGINX Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in NGINX could allow for remote code execution. NGINX is used for web serving, reverse proxying, caching, and load balancing. Exploitation could lead to remote code execution with potential impact depending on user rights.

title: New phpAfterShell Attack Bypasses PHP2Shell Fix to Enable Remote Code Execution
content: A new PHP vulnerability, phpAfterShell, allows unauthenticated remote code execution despite October patches for PHP2Shell. The flaw affects PHP’s session handler during upload progress. Applications using file-based sessions are at risk. Mitigation includes upgrading PHP and disabling session upload progress.

VMware vCenter and SDDC Manager flaws let attackers bypass authentication, gaining full control. CVSS scores range from 6.7 to 9.8. Patches are available, but no workarounds exist. Admins must apply updates and restrict network access to vCenter systems.
title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaws Let Hackers Bypass Authentication and Access Servers

content: A Russian national, Igor D'iu, was arrested for allegedly spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, conducting surveillance and collecting data via remote access devices. FBI agents found evidence linking his activities to the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB). He is charged with spying offenses and fake identity document creation.
title: Russian National Indicted for Espionage Against US Defense Tech Company in Palo Alto
JPMorgan Chase Confirms Third-Party Cyberattack That May Have Exposed Customer Names and Emails
content: A cyberattack targeted third-party service providers to JPMorgan Chase, potentially exposing customer names and email addresses. The breach did not disrupt banking services but may enable phishing attacks. Customers will receive notifications and free credit monitoring. The attack’s technical details remain unclear.

title: Protecting Against AI-Driven Attacks | Kaspersky
content: AI assistants in company computers can be exploited by attackers. Risks include unauthorized use, excessive permissions, and direct malware deployment via language models. Security measures like application control, web filtering, and threat intelligence are recommended. Response includes monitoring, allowlisting, and limiting outbound connections.

AptDeco, a high-end furniture marketplace, has faced issues with delayed payments to sellers and customer complaints. Sellers report not receiving payments for months despite products being collected. The company attributes the issue to bot swarms and is currently resolving the problem. Customers are considering legal action.
title: High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Faces Seller Payment Delays and Customer Complaints
F5 Security Advisory (AV26-1178)
content: F5 BIG-IP and related products are affected by multiple vulnerabilities. Users are advised to update to the latest versions to mitigate risks.

title: Proton Drive Adds Direct Imports from Google Drive
content: Proton Drive introduces Easy Switch for direct file imports from Google Drive, enhancing user migration. Available in Proton Drive’s web app across all plans, this feature simplifies data transfer, initially rolled out gradually.

title: OpenVPN Security Advisory (AV26-1179)
content: OpenVPN prior to 2.7.8 is affected by a vulnerability. The Cyber Centre advises users and administrators to review web links and apply necessary updates to mitigate the risk.

Google is extending the retention period of Gemini chat data to about two months, even when chat history is turned off. This change affects both temporary and newly started conversations. The update impacts user data privacy and regulatory compliance.
title: Google extends retention of Gemini chat data

content: Criminal IP launched AITEM, integrating asset discovery, public-source exposure analysis, and dark web monitoring with AI. It helps teams understand and manage exposure across their infrastructure and web assets, offering continuous monitoring and AI-assisted validation of security risks.
title: Criminal IP Launches AITEM for AI-Powered Asset Discovery and Exposure Management
Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Enables Bypass of Authentication
content: A zero-day flaw in VMware vCenter allows network attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Affects the central console for managing ESX hosts and VMs. Fixed versions available, but no workaround provided.

A critical vulnerability in Drupal core allows unauthenticated attackers to reinstall sites, potentially leading to site takeover or remote code execution. Fixed releases for all supported branches were issued. Common but uncommonly configured sites are at risk.
title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw for Unauthenticated Attackers
Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
content: Ransomware attacks involve credential theft, lateral movement, and security control disablement before data encryption. Acronis highlights five indicators to detect intrusions early, contain malicious activity, and protect systems and backups.

The PHP Foundation released security updates to fix 7 critical flaws, including remote code execution bugs. Affected deployments could be exploited. Users of all supported PHP versions should update immediately to mitigate risks.
title: PHP Addresses 7 Critical Flaws, Including Remote Code Execution Bugs

content: A study found that Black neighborhoods are twice as likely to house data centers compared to white neighborhoods. Researchers analyzed 81,000 US census tracts and 5,291 data centers, attributing the disparity to historical redlining and infrastructure placement. The study suggests data center-specific zoning and racial impact statements to address the issue.
title: Study Reveals Racial Disparities in Data Center Location
TfL breach exposed data of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers
content: A security breach compromised account details of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers. TfL has taken its portal offline and contained the incident. The breach was discovered on November 16, 2026.

PHP released critical security updates for all supported versions, addressing remote code execution and other severe vulnerabilities. Website operators and hosting providers are advised to update promptly. Vulnerabilities require uncommon setups, so risks vary. Administrators should follow the project’s changelog and patch all affected branches.
title: PHP Urges Users to Update Due to Critical Security Flaws

content: ICE is paying AT&T millions to access trillions of phone records and location data. The program likely affects AT&T customers and non-customers. Experts raise concerns over potential misuse and lack of judicial oversight.
title: ICE Pays AT&T for Access to Massive Phone Records
Meta’s AI Agent Muse Exploits Android and Mac Permissions to Read Encrypted Messages
content: Meta’s AI agent Muse read Signal messages on Android and Macs through notification and screen access, despite not directly connecting to the app. This demonstrates the technical risk of granting broad permissions to AI assistants, potentially exposing sensitive information. Users should review and limit permissions for such apps.

BADBOX 3.0 malware infected low-cost Android streaming boxes, generating 40 billion fraudulent ad requests daily. The malware played ads outside the visible screen and borrowed names of legitimate apps. It also enrolled devices in residential proxy networks. Satori Threat Intelligence identified and disrupted the campaign, recommending buyers verify Play Protect certification before purchase.
title: BADBOX 3.0 Malware Infects Android TV Boxes to Generate 40 Billion Fraudulent Ad Requests Daily

content: A Russian-speaking cybercrime operation steals login credentials for US banks, IRS, and Social Security from infected Windows PCs. Despite victims using password managers and MFA, the malware broke Chrome and Edge encryption to steal passwords. Indicators of compromise include specific server IPs and domains. Victims should use clean devices to change passwords and block listed IPs and domains.
title: Malware Steals US Bank, IRS, and Social Security Login Credentials from Infected Windows PCs
Cultural Impact of Grand Theft Auto Across Two Decades of News Coverage
content: This article chronicles how Grand Theft Auto has been covered by news media since 2001, reflecting cultural and societal changes over two decades. Initially, the games were vilified for violence and sexual content, leading to congressional hearings and moral panics. Over time, the focus shifted to the game's financial success and its role in the entertainment industry. The coverage now emphasizes economic concerns rather than moral objections. The impact on the gaming industry, including job losses, is also discussed.

CISA added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog after finding evidence of active exploitation. Affected products include Synology, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap. Exploits range from code execution to unauthorized access. Administrators should apply the latest patches and check for signs of compromise before and after updates.
title: CISA Warns Hackers Are Actively Exploiting Four Flaws in Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap

content: Google patched six critical vulnerabilities in Chrome 158, all memory-safety errors, with two found by AI. The update affects Windows, Mac, Linux, and Android. Users should update to mitigate risks.
title: Chrome Updates Patch Six Critical Flaws, Including AI-Found Bugs

content: Google released Chrome 158 with 204 security fixes, including six critical vulnerabilities found with AI. The critical flaws affect GPU, Media, WebView, and more, posing a significant risk of memory corruption. Users are advised to update Chrome to mitigate risks.
title: Google patches six critical Chrome flaws, two found with AI
Russian National Accused of Using Remote Access Tools to Spy on Silicon Valley Defense Firm
content: A Russian national was indicted for spying on a Silicon Valley defense company using remote access tools and following employees. The operation aimed to gather information about employees and their home addresses. The incident highlights the risks for defense firms and the importance of monitoring for unauthorized surveillance.

title: Attackers Exploit PHP Vulnerabilities in PAN-OS Management Interfaces
content: Attackers exploited two PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) against PAN-OS management interfaces. This allowed unauthenticated code execution on web servers. Palo Alto Networks confirmed the issue on October 28, 2023. Mitigation involves patching and securing exposed management interfaces.

title: Hackers Exploit Microsoft 365 Device Code Authentication to Hijack Accounts and Bypass MFA
content: Hackers trick employees with fake payment notices and SharePoint documents, leading them to a genuine Microsoft sign-in page and hijacking accounts. The technique does not break MFA or steal passwords. Security teams should filter authentication logs for device code flows and block them where possible. Indicators of compromise include specific domains and SHA-256 hashes.

title: Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
content: A data breach at software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details from 40 Irish credit unions. Affected credit unions reported that names, BICs, IBANs, and addresses were compromised. Wellington IT notified credit unions after the vulnerability was exploited between October 2-4, closing the flaw on October 6. The breach is criticized for delayed notification and prompts an investigation by Irish authorities.

title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for $4.5B to Enhance AI Security Solutions
content: Palo Alto Networks acquired Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to integrate AI models into its security products. The deal will enable secure, open-weight AI implementations for enterprises. Mitigation involves securing trained models and ensuring compliance with jurisdictional regulations.

A North Korea-linked hacking group, Kimsuky, used aNotepad to deliver XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT backdoors to South Korean policy and security professionals via spearphishing. The attackers switched malware without changing the initial payload, making detection challenging. They stole documents and financial details. Defenses should monitor for LNK file executions, scheduled tasks, and memory scripts.
title: Hackers Use aNotepad as a Malware Delivery Channel for XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT Backdoors
How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
content: Over the past week, multiple IT outages affected various companies and government agencies in the US, raising concerns of a cyberattack, but no evidence supports foul play. Cybersecurity analysts are needed to distinguish between technical failures and cyberattacks.

Transport for London (TfL) reported a data breach affecting around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers, with emails sent from TfL's systems misleading users. No passwords, bank details, or journey information were compromised, but customers are advised to change passwords and security questions. TfL has taken down the website for investigation and notified the ICO.
title: TfL Compromises Oyster Photocard Customer Accounts
N-able Confirms Server Breach, Disables Management Access
content: N-able confirmed unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud environment, disabling management access across three regions. Email filtering continued, but API and dashboard access were restricted. No evidence of customer data compromise found. Ongoing investigation.

A password on a sticky note led to full network access, exposing HR, salary, and accounting data. The pen tester gained access through the sticky note, showing the importance of physical security and proper access controls. The company disabled the account, reviewed logs, and tightened file share permissions.
title: Sticky note exposure leads to full network access and data theft
Ubiquiti Warns of Critical UniFi Access Flaws Enabling Root Code Execution Attacks
content: Ubiquiti disclosed seven vulnerabilities in its UniFi Access Application, allowing attackers with limited network permissions to execute code as root. Five critical flaws could lead to full host control, while others expose sensitive information or allow SSRF. Administrators should update to version 4.3.24 or later and restrict network access.

title: CISA Warns of Exploited Vulnerabilities Linked to Ransomware and Cryptomining
content: CISA warned of four exploited vulnerabilities affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt REDCap, linked to ransomware and cryptomining. Organizations are urged to update and patch systems promptly to mitigate risks.

title: Hackers Target European Commission with ARTEX AI Tool in Major Cyberattack
content: A cyberattack on the European Commission disrupted staff services for over 10 days. Hackers used an AI tool called ARTEX to target systems handling payslips, leave requests, and medical reimbursements. The extent of data access remains unclear, and the Commission is investigating. Mitigation efforts include conducting extra security checks and briefings for commissioners.
Threat actors breached N-able’s Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, disabling management interfaces and APIs. Impacted regions: 3. Mitigation efforts are underway to harden services.
title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
Scattered Spider's Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Led to Six-Year Sentence
content: Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old British man, was sentenced to six years in prison. Phishing texts and SIM swaps compromised company systems and personal accounts. Experts predict the group is fragmented but still active.

title: Scattered Spider’s Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Result in Six-Year Sentence
content: Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Tyler Robert Buchanan was sentenced to six years in prison. The group targeted at least a dozen companies and used stolen credentials to access systems. SIM swapping allowed them to take over cryptocurrency accounts. The group is fragmented, with multiple members arrested in different countries.

The cybersecurity industry has long focused on identifying and prioritizing vulnerabilities, but the real challenge is getting remediation done. Large organizations struggle with organizational bottlenecks, governance, and resource allocation. AI is increasing vulnerability discovery, but may exacerbate remediation backlogs. Effective remediation requires a robust operating model to ensure accountability and coordination across teams.
title: Vulnerability Management: The True Challenge Lies in Effective Remediation

content: A critical memory corruption flaw in Ruby’s string case conversion code allows remote code execution (RCE). Affects Ruby 3.3.0-3.3.13, 3.4.0-3.4.12, and 4.0.0-4.0.9. Exploitation can be reached through upcase, swapcase, downcase(: fold), and casecmp?. Veria Labs identified affected Ruby runtimes in popular self-hosted software like GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, and Mastodon. Updating to fixed releases is crucial to mitigate the risk.
title: Critical One-Byte Heap Overflow in Ruby Could Allow RCE Attacks
Splunk Patches Critical 9.9 RCE and Authentication Bypass Vulnerabilities in SOAR and Enterprise
content: Splunk released updates to fix critical remote code execution and authentication bypass vulnerabilities in Splunk SOAR and Enterprise. The flaws, including CVE-2026-131253 and CVE-2026-76535, require separate patches for different products. Impact includes unauthorized code execution and data access. Administrators should upgrade to the latest versions and verify patch installation.

Seven memory-safety flaws in Ruby's regular expression engine and string case-conversion code were fixed. PoCs for five flaws show remote code execution is possible. Default Rails apps are at risk. Users should update to latest versions immediately.
title: Ruby Releases Patches for Seven Memory-Safety Flaws, Some Potentially Exploitable
Hackers Deploy Overlord RAT That Survives Windows Resets and Crashes Systems When Terminated
content: A financially motivated group is deploying Overlord RAT, a Windows remote access trojan that persists after system resets and triggers a blue screen if forcefully terminated. The campaign targets cryptocurrency holders, gaming account owners, and users of internet calling software. The malware uses two persistence methods: registry entries and tampering with the Windows Recovery Environment. It also includes 35 commands for data exfiltration. Indicators of compromise include specific IP addresses and command servers.

Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14 patched seven security vulnerabilities, including RCE and buffer overflow, affecting Ruby’s regular expression engine and string case-conversion code. Users are urged to upgrade to mitigate potential attacks. Impacted versions are Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12, and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9.
title: Ruby Patches 7 Security Vulnerabilities, Including Buffer Overflow and RCE Flaws

content: Researcher shows low-privilege database accounts can be used to run code on the server via memory-corruption bugs in SQL engine code. Impacts PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and Oracle. Mitigation: Apply vendor patches, limit database privileges.
title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
Signal Introduces AI Screenshots Block to Protect Chat Privacy
content: Signal restricts AI agents from reading private chats via screenshots on Android and iOS to enhance privacy. However, the protection is incomplete. This affects users of agentic systems in iOS 27 and Android versions with encrypted messaging capabilities.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
content: Hackers exploit critical vulnerabilities in Apache, Cisco, and VMware systems for espionage. The U.S. CISA added four flaws to its KEV list, with CVE-2026-129448 rated CVSS 9.8. Affected are Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter. Organizations must patch and monitor for exploits.

title: 6 Critical F5 BIG-IP Vulnerabilities Could Let Hackers Disrupt Websites and Execute Malicious Code
content: F5 released emergency fixes for six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to crash services or execute code. These data-plane flaws impact specific configurations, affecting traffic management and potentially leading to website outages. Affected versions include BIG-IP, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes, and BIG-IP Cloud-Native Network Functions. Immediate patching and testing are advised to mitigate risks.

title: WhatsApp Android Flaws Could Let Hackers Delete Users’ Files and Expose IP Addresses
content: WhatsApp's November 2026 update addresses three flaws: file deletion, IP exposure, and a certificate check bypass. Attackers could exploit these to delete local files or expose users' IP addresses. Users should update to the latest version to mitigate risks.

PHP released patches for 18 vulnerabilities, including a critical request smuggling flaw that could enable remote code execution (RCE). Enterprises should patch all supported versions to mitigate risks, especially as PHP2Shell vulnerabilities have already caused widespread concern. Security teams must inventory and patch all PHP deployments quickly.
title: PHP2Shell Aftershock: 18 Security Flaws Patched

content: The CTO of ransomwarehelp.com, a company that purported to help victims recover encrypted data, was indicted for wire fraud. He paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and marked up the fees for victims. The company claimed to offer advanced cryptographic tools but was found to be fraudulent. This case highlights the fraudulent nature of some ransomware help services and underscores the importance of choosing reputable firms.
title: CTO of RansomwareHelp Indicted for Wire Fraud

content: F5 released out-of-band patches for BIG-IP Access Policy Manager and iRule, five of which are rated critical. These patches address stack-based buffer overflows that could lead to remote code execution. BIG-IP is used for application access management and traffic handling. F5 advises immediate hotfix installation and upgrade to patched versions to mitigate risks.
title: F5 Releases Critical Patches for BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
PHP 8.6: Addressing Remote Code Execution Flaws and Enhancing Security Defaults
content: PHP 8.6 addresses seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws, tightening session security by enabling Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite settings by default. This mitigates session hijacking and cross-site request forgery. Additionally, stricter handling of null values and other security functions are introduced to prevent data integrity issues. While these changes enhance security, administrators must ensure configurations are updated to gain full benefits.

title: Vulnerability in VMware vCenter Could Allow Authentication Bypass
content: A vulnerability in VMware vCenter could allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access, potentially leading to data manipulation or account creation with full user rights.

Visa and Mastercard suffered data breaches by ransomware and extortion group n0n, which leaked customer data including mobile numbers, BIN prefixes, and booking details. No financial details like card numbers or passwords were compromised, potentially leaving customers vulnerable to phishing attacks. Financial firms are investigating the breach, attributing it to a third-party provider, with Qubole being a suspected access path.
title: Visa, Mastercard Data Breach Lacks Financial Details but Contains Sensitive Information

content: Multiple vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab could allow arbitrary code execution. Mitel MiCollab is a unified communications platform. Successful exploitation could result in data manipulation or full system compromise. Mitigation involves timely patching and least privilege access.
title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution

content: A researcher planted 2 million digital tripwires in AI services to test for data leaks, uncovering widespread privacy violations and security breaches. Sensitive information, including AWS access keys and SSH passwords, was exposed through various AI router services. The experiment highlighted the risks in AI app development and usage, emphasizing the need for better security measures.
title: Researcher plants 2m canaries in AI supply chain to expose data leaks
Signal restricts AI agents to protect user privacy
content: Signal, an encrypted messaging app, restricts access to user messages by AI agents like Google Gemini and Apple Siri unless explicit permission is granted. This move aims to protect privacy by preventing these AI systems from accessing sensitive communications. Apple and Google are integrating AI capabilities into their operating systems, potentially compromising user data. Signal's implementation of screenshot blocking on iOS and Android apps is a partial solution, but it highlights the broader issue of AI agents undermining application privacy.
The podcast covers AI fraud, an AI agent suing Meta, and the use of AI detection tools by the Department of Justice. No clear technical incident or exploit is described.
title: Podcast Discusses AI-Driven Cyber Threats

content: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx versions 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, affecting Cisco products, were announced. These vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution and are fixed in nginx releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). CVEs include CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634. Security Impact Rating: Critical.
title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
Cisco Security Advisory - Update 1 for Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
content: Cisco is affected by multiple vulnerabilities across various products. As of November 20, 2026, CVE-2026-76466 was added to CISA's KEV database, indicating active exploitation. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates.

title: SAP Security Advisory – November 2025 Monthly Rollup (AV25-738) – Update 1
content: SAP released security advisories for multiple products in November 2025 to address vulnerabilities. CISA added a new CVE to their KEV database on November 20, 2026. Users are advised to review the advisories, apply necessary updates, and implement suggested mitigations.

title: WhatsApp Patches Security Flaws, Suspected Exploit in Android Scams
content: WhatsApp addressed 3 security flaws, one impacting Android, suspected in scam messages. CVE-2026-23871, a URL validation issue, was patched. Users should update to version 2.26.17.4.

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of HotSpot JVM on x86-64 CPUs. It allows pre-authentication remote code execution in several Java applications. OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, and versions 18 to 27, are affected. Oracle released fixed builds on November 17, 2026. Qualys offers a mitigation with TruRisk Eliminate, which automatically targets Linux and Windows hosts with AVX-512 VBMI CPUs and affected Java runtimes, adding -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS. Untested containers require manual setting of the flag.
title: Mitigating Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) with TruRisk Eliminate
Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) Exploit Mitigation via TruRisk Eliminate
content: Java4Shell is a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of the HotSpot JVM on x86-64. Affected versions include Oracle Java 17.0.6 and later, and OpenJDK 18 to 27 below the fixed builds. As of November 17, 2026, no wild exploitation has been reported, but researchers demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution. Organizations are advised to patch affected Java versions or mitigate by starting the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics. Qualys offers TruRisk Eliminate to automatically apply this mitigation on eligible hosts.

A Chinese-nexus threat actor used autonomous AI agents with Cairn to find a zero-day in an open-source medical imaging application, gaining full control of a server. The agents persisted against hardened targets for 16 hours. Defenders should prepare for rapid AI-driven attacks and prioritize automated responses.
title: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own

content: A UK government operation prevented a cyber-attack on fridges and freezers in supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations, and stadiums. The attack would have been similar to those in Europe causing significant damage. Many retailers remain vulnerable.
title: UK cybersecurity operation prevents fridge and freezer cyber-attack

content: Microsoft has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM. The recognition highlights Microsoft Sentinel’s comprehensive SIEM capabilities, including advanced analytics, automation, and threat intelligence, which help organizations protect their digital estates. Microsoft Defender’s Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) further integrates SIEM with XDR, AI, and native protection for faster threat response.
title: Microsoft Recognized as a Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM
Chinese attackers used AI to exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label
content: China-linked attackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application, gaining full control of a university server. The agents also attempted multiple other attacks before successfully exploiting the zero-day. Amazon notified the maintainers, who released a fix and advisory.

title: Microsoft Recognized as a Leader in Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
content: Microsoft was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM, highlighting its comprehensive SIEM capabilities across the digital estate. Microsoft Sentinel integrates security data, advanced analytics, automation, and threat intelligence, supporting threat hunting, investigation, and response. The Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender reimagines security operations, combining SIEM with XDR, threat intelligence, and response for faster threat detection and disruption.

Microsoft is investigating issues with attachment uploads in New Outlook. Users can work around the issue by using the Outlook on the web or classic Outlook. A fix is under development but not yet deployed.
title: Microsoft Investigates Attachment Upload Failures in New Outlook
Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays for Credential Theft and Device Control
content: A new Android malware framework called Bazuka uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices. Discovered by ThreatFabric, it integrates LLM for victim management. Affects Android users, poses significant security risks.

More than 100 Debian packages retained distrusted CA certificates after updates. This shows why trust store updates may not affect all applications. Administrators must ensure their applications use the latest trust store. Technical impact includes potential for certificate-based attacks. Mitigation involves checking and updating local trust stores.
title: Over 100 Debian Packages Still Contain Distrusted CA Certificates Despite Security Updates

content: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) warned consumers against AI-powered smart glasses due to safety concerns, including incorrect advice and privacy violations. Testing revealed issues such as dim or coverable recording lights and ability to bypass security. The AP advised banning smart glasses where necessary and called for ethical considerations in AI development.
title: Dutch Data Protection Authority Warns Against AI-Powered Smart Glasses
Behind the Blog: Keeping It Together
content: This week's Behind the Blog focuses on the online discourse surrounding a famous hippo incident, highlighting the rapid rise of expertise and toxicity in social media. No specific technical impact or affected parties are mentioned.

Moxa has released a security advisory for vulnerabilities in multiple product series, including ioLogik E1200, EDS-E, IKS, ICS, PT, SDS, TWS, and TN. Affected firmware versions are all prior to v4.0. The Cyber Centre recommends reviewing provided links and applying necessary updates.
title: Moxa issues security advisory for product vulnerabilities (AV26-1187)
Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
content: Centralized password management improves credential visibility, identifies risks, and simplifies secure sharing. Spreadsheets pose security risks by storing weak, reused, or compromised credentials outside approved systems.

Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: EU sanctions NoName057(16), malware targets CACs, Gemini agents targeted Epoch AI. Impact on cybersecurity landscape, potential for broader threats.
title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit
Noteworthy Cybersecurity Stories
content: EU sanctions NoName057(16), malware targets CACs, and Gemini agents hit. Multiple unrelated cybersecurity incidents reported.

title: Critical Apache Tomcat Flaw Lets Remote Attackers Join Trusted Server Clusters Without Authentication
content: A critical flaw in Apache Tomcat allows remote attackers to join trusted server clusters without authentication. This affects versions 11.0.28-29 and 10.1.62-9.0.124 when using TLS 1.3 with a pre-shared key. Apache recommends switching to TLS 1.2 and updating to fixed versions pending release. Mitigation involves checking cluster settings and reviewing logs.

title: US launches center to disrupt scams and warn victims sooner
content: The US establishes the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies for rapid intervention against scams. It aims to freeze funds, take down malicious domains, and ban scammers’ accounts. Beneficiaries include cryptocurrency users, social network users, and victims of cybercrime. Early reporting to the FBI’s IC3 is crucial for effective response.

title: US Launches Threat Disruption Center to Combat Scams
content: The US launches the Threat Disruption Center to connect investigators with companies to interrupt scam infrastructure and help victims. The center aims to freeze funds, take down malicious domains, and ban scammers’ accounts. Beneficiaries include anyone targeted by scams, cybercrime, and sextortion. Victims are advised to report scams immediately to the FBI’s IC3.

title: Signal restricts screenshots to prevent AI assistants from accessing private chats
content: Signal updated iOS 27 and Android devices to block screenshots to avoid AI assistants like Siri and Gemini from reading private conversations. This update extends previous protections against Microsoft Recall. The change aims to safeguard user privacy.

Hackers spread malware through fake GTA 6 PC launchers on 355 domains. Victims downloading the ZIP archive run malicious programs. Security teams should monitor DNS and web proxy logs for IoCs and verify downloads through official channels.
title: Hackers Use 355 Domains to Spread Fake GTA 6 PC Launchers Delivering Malware
Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers
content: A ransomware group leaked data including emails, phone numbers, and travel or dining bookings from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers. No payment data was exposed. Companies acknowledged incidents but reported no impact to their payment networks. Customers should verify messages and use Malwarebytes Scam Guard to protect their accounts.

A ransomware group leaked customer data from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. The data includes emails, phone numbers, and travel or dining bookings. Cybercriminals could exploit this information for phishing attacks. JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard reported no impact to payment networks, but the leak poses risks to customer security.
title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers

content: Hackers modified the SoftEther VPN Bridge, known as NtMonitor, to quietly link external networks to victim’s local networks, aiding espionage. Linked to Webworm, a China-aligned group, this tool was used post-breach to maintain access without detection. Defenders should inventory approved services, monitor unexpected services, and collect IoCs for analysis.
title: Hackers Rebuild Legitimate VPN Software for Espionage

content: A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability in OpenSSL’s Base64 encoding function can corrupt application memory when processing large inputs. This flaw affects versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.3 and 4.1.0, with fixes in 4.0.4 and 4.1.1. Security teams should check for untrusted data usage and enforce input limits before encoding, ensuring all OpenSSL copies across systems, containers, and applications are updated and verified.
title: OpenSSL Hit by Critical 9.8 Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in Base64 Encoding Function

content: A vulnerability in KVM, the Linux hypervisor, lets guest VMs access host memory on AMD-hosted servers. This affects DigitalOcean shared servers with nested virtualization. The flaw, CVE-2026-99312, was exploited to read about 127 GB of memory. Mitigation involves updating to fixed kernels.
title: KVM Hypervisor Vulnerability CVE-2026-99312 Allows Guest VMs to Access Host Memory
AI Autonomy in Security Operations
content: Security leaders are increasing the autonomy of AI agents in low-risk security actions. By 2027, 60% expect to be comfortable with autonomous AI. The shift aims to enhance efficiency in Security Operations Centers (SOC).

title: UK Court Forces Government to Admit Demanding Apple iCloud Backdoor
content: The UK Investigatory Powers Tribunal confirmed the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. Apple’s decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection for UK users was seen as indirect confirmation. The government argues it is necessary for national security, but Apple opposes, emphasizing customer privacy. A substantive hearing is scheduled for 2027.

Ransomware hackers used audio messages to demand ransom from multiple institutions, causing operational disruptions. The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center and Vanderbilt University experienced audio demands, with the latter ordering a device shutdown. BYOD claimed to have compromised 36,000 systems and stole over a million Social Security numbers. Victims faced unexpected login prompts and credential compromises. Mitigation includes checking logs, testing backups, and reporting unsolicited messages.
title: BYOD Ransomware Hackers Play Audio Ransom Messages on Computers Across Hospitals and Universities

content: Attackers are using an AI-driven testing tool called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks by finding and exploiting ordinary mistakes in company networks. This tool has been used by criminals and state-linked groups since at least August 2026. It can reach privileged access in under three hours. Defenders should limit exposed APIs, set WAF rules, and use disposable VMs for testing to mitigate risks.
title: Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX Framework to Automate Cyberattacks Without Relying on Zero-Day Exploits

content: A vulnerability in Windows 11 passkey authentication can trigger error messages on Android devices even after a successful sign-in. A fix has been released for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. The issue impacts cross-device authentication using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager. Until patched, users can ignore errors if authentication succeeds on the PC.
title: Windows 11 passkey bug causes authentication failure messages
SonicWall Urges Replacement of Gen 6 Firewalls Due to Security Risks
content: SonicWall advises retiring Generation 6 firewalls due to security risks from AI-assisted attacks. Customers are urged to replace and stop exposing these devices on the internet to mitigate vulnerabilities. Technical impact includes increased risk of exploitation by attackers using automation and AI.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
content: Threat actors exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway, to breach a Russian organization. The breach involved four devices and provided access to the internal network. CVSS score: 9.8.

title: No Straight Lines: The value of a different career journey
content: No straight lines: career changes, breaks, and diverse industry experience build resilience, curiosity, and perspective. Communities support career transitions, recognizing transferable skills. Diverse journeys strengthen inclusive teams in tech.

title: BADBOX 3.0 malware used Android TV boxes for ad fraud
content: BADBOX 3.0 malware compromised Android TV boxes to generate 40 billion daily bid requests for ad fraud. This affected homeowners whose internet connections were sold for advertising. The technical impact included unauthorized use of devices for hidden video ads and increased advertiser competition. Mitigation involved disrupting the operation.

title: Signal Restricts Screenshots to Protect User Privacy from AI Assistants
content: Signal is restricting screenshots on iOS 27 and some Android devices to prevent AI assistants from reading private chats. The change targets Apple’s Siri and Google Gemini, addressing the risk of AI assistants capturing message text post-delivery. Users can turn off the protection in privacy settings but exposing messages to other people in the chat is a risk.

The UK’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal confirmed a secret order from the Home Office to Apple for access to encrypted iCloud data. This decision rejects the government’s attempt to keep the order secret, highlighting potential cybersecurity and privacy risks.
title: UK tribunal confirms secret Apple order in iCloud encryption dispute

content: The Digital Café helps the Nauheim community build technology confidence. Sophos volunteers provide 40 hours of paid leave for the initiative, enhancing digital inclusion. No technical impact or mitigation details available.
title: Empowering Employees to Make a Difference: The Digital Café
Palo Alto Confirms Critical Java Vulnerability Affects Privilege Threat Analytics and Remote Access Connector
content: A critical Java vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) affects Palo Alto Networks products, enabling remote code execution under specific conditions. Affected products include Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector, and on-premises HTML5 Gateway. Customers should upgrade to the latest versions. The vulnerability is rated CVSS 9.2 and requires Java running on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI support and specific configurations.

ClamAV released versions 1.5.5 and 1.4.7 to address 10 high-severity vulnerabilities that could crash antivirus scanners, cause endless loops, or drain system resources. Affected components include email handling, document parsing, and archive extraction. Attackers could exploit these flaws to disrupt scanning availability or gain unauthorized access. Administrators should update to the latest versions to mitigate these risks.
title: ClamAV Patches 10 High-Severity Vulnerabilities That Could Let Attackers Crash Antivirus Scanners

content: Transport for London (TfL) detected a breach on its Oyster photocard website, exposing personal information of 265,000 customers, including email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth. TfL advised customers to change matching passwords or security answers used on other accounts. The breach did not compromise passwords, bank details, or payment card information.
title: Hackers Breach TfL Oyster Photocard Accounts, Exposing Personal Data of 265,000 Customers

content: Hackers exploited misconfigured Temenos Quantum Fabric to deploy web shells without passwords, gaining admin access via a misconfigured authentication service. Affected financial institutions across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The exploit used custom Java integrations to gain access to application and database connections. Defenders should check for unexpected Java packages and service imports, and log suspicious activities.
title: Hackers Exploit Misconfigured Temenos Banking Platform to Deploy Web Shells Without Passwords
Chase says vendor cyberattack may have exposed customer data
content: Attackers targeted third-party vendors, potentially exposing customer names and email addresses. Chase, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed incidents after data was stolen and posted online. Mitigation involves monitoring and tightening vendor security.

title: AI's Mathematical Advances Spark Debate on Public-Key Cryptography Security
content: A cryptographer warns that existing public-key cryptography systems may fail due to AI advancements, posing a threat to PKI. Experts debate the need for immediate action or gradual modernization. The main concern is that AI could find shortcuts to solving hard mathematical problems underlying PKI. While some suggest cautious improvement, others recommend following established modernization paths.

title: Hackers Actively Scan LiteLLM AI Servers for Critical Flaws Enabling RCE Attacks
content: Attackers are scanning LiteLLM servers for two vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710) to gain remote code execution (RCE) without authentication. The first flaw allows execution of commands with the proxy’s privileges, while the second bypasses login checks. Exploits target the /mcp-rest/test/tools/list path and use crafted Host headers. Affected servers can expose API keys and cloud access. Mitigation includes patching and restricting public access. Teams should rotate keys and review logs for suspicious activity.

Threat actors use ROMULUS ClickFix to deploy a new remote access trojan (RAT) similar to CNCMachineRMS. It allows spying and PC control. Affected users are targeted via malware delivery. Mitigation involves updating systems and monitoring for unauthorized access.
title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs

content: Hackers used 41 AI-assisted PowerShell modules to search for credentials and test API access at an unnamed African stock exchange. Six persistence implants linked to Witchetty, a China-linked espionage group, were found. Indicators of compromise included DNS queries and unusual web server activity. Security teams should monitor DNS logs and compare them with endpoint and authentication logs for signs of intrusion.
title: Hackers Deploy AI-Assisted PowerShell Toolkit to Target African Stock Exchange

content: Wireshark 4.6.10 addresses 39 security vulnerabilities, including crashes, processing loops, memory leaks, and heap disclosures affecting protocol dissectors and capture file parsers. Teams should update to mitigate risks, especially where external capture files are analyzed.
title: Wireshark 4.6.10 Released With Patch for 39 Security Vulnerabilities

content: Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) in VMware vCenter Server, gaining admin access and stealing data. Affects VMware vCenter users. Mitigation: Apply patches immediately.
title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
Hackers Leak Customer Data Linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan After Third-Party Cyberattacks
content: Hackers published customer data from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. No breaches occurred at the financial companies themselves. The data exposure included names, email addresses, and other marketing details, potentially impacting thousands of customers. Companies are investigating vendor breaches and offering support.

title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
content: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock allows physical access users to run programs on a locked Windows PC without signing in, gaining only limited account access. The method was posted by researchers MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, impacting Windows systems until a patch is applied.

title: Drupal Fixes Critical RCE Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated Takeover
content: Drupal released updates to fix a critical RCE flaw, enabling unauthenticated attackers to take over vulnerable sites. The installer bug affects Drupal core versions and could lead to remote code execution. Administrators must update to the latest version to mitigate risk.

title: KPMG Canada Confirms Cyberattack as Hackers Access Confidential Client Tax Documents
content: KPMG Canada confirmed a cybersecurity breach where confidential tax documents of some clients were accessed. Immediate actions included containment and communication with affected clients. The nature and extent of the breach remain unclear, as details on the type of data accessed are not disclosed. Clients should verify information and monitor their accounts for unusual activity.

title: Critical Zero-Day in Windows Package Manager Exposes Microsoft’s Software Supply Chain
content: A zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft’s Windows Package Manager (WinGet) allowed a single pull request to potentially compromise moderator credentials, exposing a significant supply chain risk. The flaw, present in the internal triage tool, could allow attackers to access and modify Microsoft repositories, including pushing backdoored installers. Microsoft has patched the vulnerability, but the underlying credential model is criticized as fundamentally flawed. Enterprises must review their automation tools and replace broad, long-lived tokens with narrow, short-lived ones to mitigate similar risks.

Around 8.8 million NGINX services may still be exposed to a critical set of five memory bugs. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote users to run commands as the NGINX worker process. The most severe bug, CVE-2026-123007, affects all NGINX versions from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8. Patching or disabling HTTP/2 is recommended to mitigate the risk. No exploitation has been reported in the wild as of 18 November 2026.
title: 8.8 Million NGINX Services Potentially Exposed to Critical NGINX2Root Vulnerability

content: A suspected China-linked espionage group exploited a VMware vCenter Server zero-day in September 2026, gaining admin access and stealing files from a Windows VM. The group used custom tools and stole encryption material and database credentials. Patching is required, but does not fully mitigate the threat.
title: Hackers Exploit VMware vCenter 0-Day Since September to Hijack Admin Accounts and Steal VM Data

content: The European Commission HR systems were compromised by attackers using the ARTEX penetration testing tool. The attack forced the Commission to temporarily shut down access for over 10 days. No evidence of a data breach was found, but the attackers are suspected to have searched for and located credentials. HR systems, containing sensitive information, were targeted, making them a valuable prize for espionage and social engineering. Mitigation includes checking other systems and defining secure fallback processes.
title: European Commission HR systems hit by cyber attack using ARTEX tool
New Windows 11 Narrator Lock Screen 0-Day Allows Attackers to Bypass BitLocker Protections
content: A newly disclosed Windows 11 zero-day called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access bypass parts of the Windows lock screen and run code without signing in, potentially exposing a running PC even when BitLocker is enabled. The issue affects Narrator and requires at least one user account linked to an online Microsoft account. Microsoft has not issued a patch as of the reporting date. Teams should limit physical access to exposed devices and watch for an advisory.

title: VMware and KVM Vulnerabilities Require Urgent Attention
content: VMware published critical advisories for two vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123890 and CVE-2026-123891) in vCenter and SDDC Manager, allowing unauthorized access and command execution. Additionally, KVM has a CVE-2026-99312 that enables DoS and memory corruption attacks on hosts with AMD processors. Mitigation involves applying patches and disabling nested virtualization where applicable.

Germ Network, a new encrypted messaging client, launched its Android version, seeing a 20x jump in usage since its iOS release. The app uses end-to-end encryption and a unique card system for identity management, aiming to provide more control over shared information. Collaboration with Bluesky and AT Protocol supports its growth, but Germ plans to introduce premium features later. Security and privacy are top concerns, with efforts to minimize metadata and avoid AI integration risks.
title: Germ Network Launches Android Version of Encrypted Messaging App
AWS re:Invent 2026 Security and Governance Sessions
content: AWS invites attendees to re:Invent 2026 for security, identity, and governance sessions.
